sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Owein, also written Owain, Iwein, or Yvain, is an Arthurian hero. In the Welsh text the Dream of Rhonabwy this name belongs to a knight of Camelot, son of king Urien and of king Arthur's sorceress half-sister Morgan. On his travels Owein heard of a land tormented by a strange Black Knight. He followed the Knight to a forest, Brocéliande, and defeated him. There he found a fountain guarded by the maiden Luned, who helped him win the heart of her mistress, the Lady of the Fountain. Owein swore to remain true but broke his word, leaving to travel with Arthur and forgetting to come back. Luned trailed him to Camelot and shamed him before the knights for his faithlessness. He fled into the forest, healed himself, and became a knight once more. He then freed Luned from a giant who had taken her. In return Luned brought Owein back together with the Lady of the Fountain.

okr.objective: Owein is an Arthurian knight who wins and loses a lady's love.
